## What's New?

The release of Unreal Engine 5.8 brings further improvements to the UE5 toolset. This release delivers improvements in a wide variety of areas, including Rendering, Character and Animation, Worldbuilding, PCG, and more.

This release includes improvements submitted by our community of Unreal Engine developers on GitHub. Thank you to each of these contributors to Unreal Engine 5.8:

ABostrom, adam-struge-cdpr, AHGS-Jens, AlexanderVeselov-arm, alexdjq, AlexKenkenbergMetrea, Almax27, AMcClean97, Armageddon-15, aziogroup, ben-mkiv, BibbitM, BlackMATov, BlueMountainsIO, bohdon, byjtew, byte-warlock, cneumann, ColinGulliver, daktor, Damon3000s, Darcy3000s, davidesocol, dman82499, dthex5d, dyanikoglu, dzianisbutsianouski-cdpr, Edstub207, Epiphane, erebel55, Erlandys, filipkoperski, funfoofi, gamethread, Gearbox-SFatnassi, h13jc, HSeo, hugebug4ever, Iannis623, iniside, intvoker, Itotallyhavememes, ivorne, jacksonhvisuals, Jal1338, jdamdami, jeremy-skymap, JiayinCaoNV, JonnyTsGitHub, jorgenpt, JRProdSD, KaizerDragomir, kiruru002, kjohnsonTNM, kroopson, kumikai-nick, l-t-m-f, lapislosh, lclara-BARB, leeejongmin, LightKL, luciddream-tsin, Maigo, MarkJGx, Marvelius, megesdal, melku, mfgoleleka, microneo, mikeseese, mrobitaille-riot, Murazaki, nils-soderman, nrs-cerickson, Ogniok, pafuhana1213, peterschusteratms, PICO-XR, pigi5, PR3C14D0, ProdigyThirteen, PushStartInteractive, rdunnington, RedFlowering, redxdev, Riopho, riotcam, RKIV, rmatteson-riot-personal, rokenrock, ronaldogsk, Sage-of-Mirrors, sareali, SimonLeeGit, skokon, Skylonxe, slonopotamus, SoulSharer, SRombauts, ssutherland-riot, TeamBaconn, TheJSLo, tomilov, Vaei, Variann, VesCodes, x380kkm, yaakuro, yangskyboxlabs, yicwang25, zompi2

## Rendering

### Megalights

![Megalights](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/90936c32-5506-4c8c-bf6e-ac80be6854cb?resizing_type=fit)

**Megalights** is now entering Production Ready status with Unreal Engine 5.8. We greatly reduced noise to maximize visual fidelity, while also improving overall performance to achieve 60fps. We also introduced new tooling to help debug and optimize your scenes.

**Features Support**

- Transmission support (subsurface scattering)

- New Froxel-based translucency support

- High quality front layer translucency lighting

- IES support for volumetrics and translucency

- Lighting channels support

- Cloud shadows

- First-person perspective weapon support


**Visualization Views**

- Light finder tool (debugging and optimization)

- Ray visualizer tool (ray iteration count)

- Shadow caster and shadow caster mismatch view


For more information on this feature, see [MegaLights](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/megalights-in-unreal-engine).

### Lumen Lite (Beta)

![Lumen Medium Quality](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/92725b02-d1f1-43d7-89ad-91c26fc1bcce?resizing_type=fit)

Lumen Lite is a new medium-quality setting for Global Illumination using Irradiance Fields with Probe Occlusion supported by Lumen. It's twice as fast as Lumen high quality - which targets 60fps on PlayStation 5, while maintaining the art direction for games that rely on Global Illumination. This path is the new default for current-generation handheld consoles, where it can be used at 60fps, and it is supported on PC as well.

For more information on this feature, see [Lumen Technical Details](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/lumen-technical-details-in-unreal-engine) and [Lumen Performance Guide](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/lumen-performance-guide-for-unreal-engine).

### X-Rite AXF Materials as Substrate

![X-Rite AXF Materials as Substrate](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/cca83e1b-419e-47c9-b50c-23f233ce697d?resizing_type=fit)

We’re adding support for importing measured materials from X-Rite’s AxF format into Unreal Engine, using the Substrate material system.

This feature gives automotive and industrial visualization teams a way to bring high-fidelity, real-world scanned materials—exported from X-Rite Pantora—directly into Unreal Engine.

### FSSS - Fog Screen Space Scattering (Experimental)

![FSSS - Fog Screen Space Scattering](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/32c7f330-a629-482b-a3cd-3872d7897569?resizing_type=fit)

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we introduce an experimental **Fog Screen Space Scattering (FSSS)** feature on the Exponential Height Fog component that approximates multiple light scattering within participating media—making dense fog, smoke, and dust appear blurrier and more integrated with the scene by simulating how light scatters through volumetric effects.

It supports all Volumetric Fog and Local Fog Volumes, with configurable controls for scene color integration and scattering spread, though Volumetric Clouds and Heterogeneous Volumes are not yet supported. As an experimental feature it currently offers only a single blur quality level and may exhibit visual artifacts.

### Substrate NPR Shading (Experimental)

![Substrate NPR Shading](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/52b48e32-e8a0-4d93-bbae-41541d78213b?resizing_type=fit)

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we introduce experimental **Substrate Toon Shading**, a stylized non-photorealistic rendering solution built on the Substrate Blendable GBuffer (legacy) mode. It supports all light types including local lights, sky lights, and Lumen global illumination, and exposes precise control over diffuse and specular response through a new Substrate Toon BSDF and Toon Profile asset.

Substrate NPR shading features include ramp-based diffuse and specular control with dithering, self-shadowing extinction with hatching patterns, anisotropic specular highlights, and global illumination scale controls.

## Character and Animation

### Modular Control Rig Improvements

![Modular Control Rig Improvements](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/5b36d4e0-907c-4199-acc3-71b4256233ae?resizing_type=fit)

In Unreal Engine 5.8, we’ve focused on improving stability and day-to-day usability of Modular Control Rig. These updates address long-standing friction in hierarchy management, module authoring, connector workflows, and mirroring behavior.

#### Display

- New **Show Empty Sockets Only** viewport option that simplifies dragging and dropping modules and helps enable building sockets on top of modules.


#### Hierarchy and State Persistence

Improved reliability and consistency of the rig and module hierarchies:

- Rig hierarchy and module hierarchy now reliably retain state after compilation.

- Fixed an issue where interacting with class settings in rig modules could cause the rig hierarchy to disappear.

- Resolved an undo/redo issue that could clear the entire rig hierarchy.

- Modular hierarchy filter settings now persist across sessions.

- Fixed an issue where selected controls could remain stuck after compiling dependent modules.

- Schematic Viewport visibility now persists across editor sessions.

- Module rig class fields now display both asset name and full asset path.

- Shift-click and MMB-click now expand or collapse children in the module hierarchy.

- Module hierarchy tree is now more compact and readable.

- Module hierarchy search now includes module class when that column is visible.

- Added options to show or hide the Connector and Module Class columns.

- Added hotkeys to show/hide optional, secondary, and unresolved connectors in the module hierarchy.


#### Module Authoring and Creation Workflow

Streamlined common authoring tasks and improved discoverability:

- Modules can now be duplicated using a right-click in the module hierarchy.

- Added a hotkey for duplicating modules.

- Dragging and dropping modules now automatically enables schematic view.

- Added Control Rig Module to the Create Control Rig Asset menu.

- Added a hotkey for creating new sockets.


#### Connector System Improvements

Significant quality-of-life and rule-handling improvements for connectors:

- Shape Types are now selectable from a dropdown in the Modular Rig editor.

- Connector descriptions defined in a control rig module now appear as tooltips.

- Array connector reorder handles are now visible by default.

- Non-draggable connectors display a plug icon and show connections via tooltip.

- Enabled drag-and-drop of connectors directly from the Details panel.

- Added support for showing/hiding connector and module class in the hierarchy.

- Delete all now correctly clears array entries in the Details panel.

- Fixed inability to remove all connections from array connectors.

- Fixed non-array connectors incorrectly appearing as arrays in Details.

- Added min/max rule support for connector arrays.

- Added Set Default Match support for connector arrays (supports single connectors and wildcard arrays).

- Enabled adding default targets to empty array connectors.

- Prevented full hierarchy and Details panel refresh when editing array connectors.

- Improved connector resolution when duplicating modules with child modules.

- Connector selection now correctly respects connector rules in module details.

- Fixed a rare crash when editing connector rules in control rig modules.


#### Mirroring Improvements

- Modular rigs now retain mirror input settings.

- Mirror modules now correctly mirror sub-hierarchies and multi-selection.


### Skeletal Editor Blendshape Rigging Tools

![Skeletal Editor Blendshape Rigging Tools](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/eccf0cc7-0f60-4d61-b577-4d8db7798476?resizing_type=fit)

#### Rigging and Blendshape Tools

Expanded face rigging and morph target editing tools in Unreal Engine 5.8 extend the Skeletal Editor and Control Rig to better support sculpt-driven facial workflows. These improvements strengthen in-engine blendshape authoring for stylized characters, custom skeletal meshes, and MetaHumans.

- Joint locking support during skinning workflows.

- Mesh element selection and editing for morph targets, with soft selection support.

- Hotkey to mirror (symmetrize) morph targets.

- Menu option to flip morph targets.

- New tool to split a morph target into two using a vertex map.

- Lattice deformer for morph target editing.

- Post-process geometry script for LOD generation (enabling simplified subdivision-style workflows).

- More consistent Move Brush behavior.

- Surface-based brush falloff.


We made quality-of-life improvements across Skeletal Editor tools to improve stability, usability, and production workflows.

#### Selection

- Maintain vertex/component selection when exiting Isolate Selected.

- Ctrl+click on buttons switches to new selection mode.

- Shift+click buttons to modify existing selections.

- Select bones directly from the Weights Component editor.

- Integration with the new unified gizmo system for asset editors.


#### Skinning and Weight Editing

- Fixed issue where adding weights to bones did not properly update the skeleton tree.

- Updated weight paint ramp widgets.

- Significant weighting tool improvements aligned with blendshape workflow development.

- New skin weight locking functionality.

  - Adjust weights between two influences without affecting others.

#### Bone Editing

- Mirror strings now work anywhere in the bone name.

- Support for mirroring joints across hierarchies.

- Fixed bone renaming issues.

- Fixed skeleton tree child selection visibility when collapsing hierarchies.

- Axis dropdown no longer incorrectly allows None.

- Added Local Rotation Axis (LRA) debug display.

- Added Orient Selected Bones Only option.

- Added Paste Special options for transferring joints between assets.

- Moved the Mesh and Bones menu to the top viewport toolbar.


#### Mesh and Morph Editing

- Added basic mesh element editing for base meshes and morph targets.

  - Currently supports moving selected elements.

  - Foundation for expanded editing capabilities.

#### Bone Count Reduction Tool

- New option to remove unused bones from skeletal meshes.

  - Removes bones not referenced by skin weights.

  - Preserves parent hierarchy to root.

### Animate with Control Rig Physics (Beta)

![Animate with Control Rig Physics](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/2d37cb4c-7675-462c-9933-e5d0a89abfc0?resizing_type=fit)

**Control Rig Physics** moves to Beta, this release introduces new force-based functionality and expanded tooling to enable more physics-driven animation workflows.

Physics rigs now behave as layered rigs, compositing naturally on top of existing animation without requiring an explicit layered rig setup.

These updates enhance both rig authoring and animator-facing usability, particularly within Modular Control Rig.

**What's New:**

- Support for applying forces directly within Control Rig Physics.

- Ability to animate forces over time for dynamic rig behavior.

- Runtime performance improvements.

- Improvements to the way “alpha” works to blend between simulation and pass-through.

- New physics modules for Modular Control Rig to simplify physics setup.

- New physics utility rigs in the animator kit to assist animators working with physics-driven rigs.


These improvements expand the creative range of physics-based rigging.

### Dynamics - Particle Based Physics for Control Rig

![Dynamics - Particle Based Physics for Control Rig](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/17162b95-bd6f-4705-92c0-322c54dd3081?resizing_type=fit)

**Control Rig Dynamics** is a new, lightweight particle-based solver built directly into Control Rig for high-performance in-game character simulations.

This plugin is designed for fast, authorable physics for cosmetic elements like clothing, hair, and accessories without the overhead of full physics engine capabilities.

**What's New:**

- New Control Rig Dynamics plugin with a dedicated particle-based solver built for real-time performance.

- 5x runtime performance improvement over existing physics solutions.

- Fewer nodes and a simplified authoring workflow to reduce setup complexity.

- Purpose-built for in-game cosmetics and physics-driven character assets.


Control Rig Dynamics gives technical animators and riggers a fast, practical path to physics-based character simulation.

### Animate with Direct Mesh Controls (Experimental)

![](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/54ffdcdf-07bf-417f-80be-5b47d3c43bc0?resizing_type=fit)

**Direct Mesh Controls (DMC)** enable control rig controls to be represented directly on sections of the skeletal mesh, giving animators a way to manipulate rigs by interacting with the character surface in-context. This introduces a new control paradigm that complements traditional static shape controls.

- Creation of mesh-based control groups that function as control rig controls.

- Direct selection and manipulation of mesh regions in the viewport and Sequencer.

- Co-existence with traditional static shape controls for rigs where mesh controls are not appropriate (for example, tails, mechanical rigs).

- Viewport-driven click-and-drag interaction for faster object and rig manipulation.

We synchronized selection across Sequencer, Curve Editor, and the Viewport.

- Selection is now fully synchronized across the Viewport, Sequencer, and Curve Editor. Click a control on the character in the Viewport, pick a track in the Sequencer outliner, or select a curve in the Curve Editor — all three panels update together, instantly, every time.

- All your filters and searches are linked now by default as well. So anything you do in one of the editors is reflected in the other.

- The new Link icon lets you decide if you want this linked behavior or not.. When in an unlinked state you can decide what you're looking at in either view.

Sequencer can now collapse down to a simplified view to give artists the freedom to focus on parts of the viewport while authoring animations.

  - Hotkey to hide toolbar (shift-backspace)
- Functionality

  - Snapping to frame and smart snap support
- Curated toolbar for character animation authoring

  - Add/remove in-betweens
- Options

  - Grid color blocks

  - Show/hide toolbar, transport controls, range slider

We added new workflows for automatically baking to animation sequences and swapping back and forth between baked data and live control rig data..

- Added a new Configure AutoBake option to the right-click menu.

- Takes advantage of the linked animation sequences workflow.

- Added a quick toggle icon to anything that is configured with this autobake.


### Animation Mixing in Sequencer (Experimental)

![Animation Mixing in Sequencer](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/2535fb5d-b58c-4d9d-9187-65a523b056a2?resizing_type=fit)

Expanding on the work done in 5.6 on seamless gameplay transition for cinematics, the **Animation Mixer** augments cinematic artists' ability to mix different animation input directly within Sequencer. This gives cinematic artists a way to layer and mask character animations for their sequences, without having the need of a separate animation Blueprint or specific slots. The Animation Mixer also supports workflows for the new Unreal Animation Framework.

With it, you can:

- Create animation mixers to assign to animation Blueprint slots or custom animation instances.

- Create mix layers to layer skeletal animation, control rig, or any input that affect the skeletal pose in a priority order.

- Mask bones and curves with a blend mask asset on any mix layer.

- Add modifiers to any mixer, layer, or section to bone match, offset root motion, mirroring, and more.

- Add transitions such as cross fading or dead blending between animations.


### Foot Definition for Retargeting

![Foot Definition for Retargeting](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/d3a5bd5f-e39a-4eb9-a953-a6d6a0f81a4d?resizing_type=fit)

For Unreal Engine 5.8, we continue to improve IK Retargeter, transferring foot animations across a wide variety of characters. Artists focusing on both runtime retargeting and motion capture workflows can use these new abilities to confidently get great results when retargeting to different characters. For more information, see [Foot Settings in the Retargeter Operations Stack documentation](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/retargeting-operation-stack-in-unreal-engine-5-8#foot-settings).

- Define a foot plane and toes for the target character for better controlled transfers.

- Auto retargeting templates for retarget chains updated for foot definition.

- Additional control to prevent dampening of vertical pelvis motion on shorter characters

- Blend to Source, Scale Goals, and Offset Goals are split out in the IK Op Stack for more flexibility in ordering.


### Retarget Override Sets

![Retarget Override Sets](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/2e9d0c34-de75-4544-b111-15bb31586c51?resizing_type=fit)

For gameplay retargeting workflows, **Retarget Override Sets** make it possible for a single IK retargeter asset to handle different retarget relationships without additional asset creation or extra Blueprint logic. For more information, see [Override Sets in the IK Rig Retargeting documentation](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/ik-rig-animation-retargeting-in-unreal-engine#override-sets).

- Author a collection of ops and their properties to store as a retarget override set in the retargeter asset.

- Add and inherit from existing override sets for more flexible retargets.

- Bind ops and/or their properties to an animation curve or a variable in an override set.

- Set which override set to use when running IK retargeter for runtime retargeting or offline retargeting.


For more information on this feature, see [IK Rig Retargeting](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/ik-rig-animation-retargeting-in-unreal-engine).

### RigMapper Animation Retargeting Tool (Beta)

![RigMapper Animation Retargeting Tool](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/5283b7f4-a54a-4a47-876c-777dd683257f?resizing_type=fit)

We're continuing to improve **Rig Mapper** with better node graph authoring capabilities and further integration within the IK Retargeter to handle more completed facial animation transfers. It provides a way to transfer motion between different character setups, such as applying ARKit animations to MetaHumans or using MetaHuman Animator (MHA) animations on ARKit characters.

We expanded **remap curves** to a stack of ops to handle all curve retargeting operations in a priority order.

- The previous 5.7 workflow is now supported with the user data rig mapper op that handles rig mapper evaluation in array order.

- We provided a new single rig mapper op for users to assign a single rig mapper definition.

  - Create multiple single rig mapper ops in the remap curves stack to determine priority order of evaluation.
- We expanded the Rig Mapper Definition editor's nodal graph behaviors for a better user experience:

  - Create new nodes from the context menu or by dragging and dropping pins.

  - Drag and connect pins from node to node with contextual and directional awareness.

  - Move and arrange groups of nodes.

  - Updated the Details panel for every node with real-time edits visible in the graph.

### Mutable

![Mutable](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/ff69b4fc-03b4-48a8-88bb-8c2d4135654f?resizing_type=fit)

**Mutable** in UE 5.8 release reaches production readiness with stability, performance, and pipeline improvements.

Dataless customizable objects enable runtime-driven parameter handling for faster iteration, graph reusability, and better patching. They are optimized for mesh operations and simple texture composition.

Dataless workflows provide a way to evaluate parameter inputs at runtime instead of compile time, significantly reducing iteration cost while maintaining compatibility with Unreal Engine's packaging and encryption systems.

Skeletal mesh pin simplifies common workflows by giving users a way to work at the skeletal mesh level instead of mesh sections.

We made performance improvements across the board, including parallel updates to boost generation throughput for crowds, reduced game thread workload, and optimized mesh and texture operations.

For more information on this feature, see [Mutable Skeletal Mesh Generation](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/mutable-skeletal-mesh-generation-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.5).

### Live Link Face Video Streaming

Live Link Face on iOS and Android now streams video in real time directly to Unreal Engine, enabling on-set supervisors and directors to monitor an actor's performance as it happens. The video stream integrates with Unreal Engine Media Profiles, allowing you to review captured footage alongside solved animation. On newer devices, video streaming and real-time animation solving run simultaneously. The stream is designed to work reliably on low-bandwidth, high-latency Wi-Fi networks.

## MetaHuman

### Populate Your World with a MetaHuman Crowd

![MetaHuman Crowd in UE](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/c196f37f-6542-4027-90f8-63cb706cc523?resizing_type=fit)

Assemble optimized instances of MetaHuman characters to [create crowds](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/metahuman/metahuman-crowds-in-unreal-engine) compatible with Mass, scaling from tens to thousands of characters. The new experimental MetaHuman Crowd plugin provides a complete assembly pipeline with seamless transitions between high-fidelity individual actors and lower-fidelity Instanced Skeletal Meshes based on camera distance.

**Key Features:**

- Build collections of modular components (head, body, hair, clothing) and compose them by hand or procedurally using Blueprints.

- Optimized face textures that maintain visual fidelity with reduced memory footprint.

- Animation applied using Unreal Animation Framework or simple sequences depending on distance.

- Simulated with Mass, rendered using Nanite or dynamic LOD systems.

- Example project setup available separately, runs on all Unreal Engine target platforms.


For more information on this feature, see [MetaHuman Crowds](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/metahuman/metahuman-crowds-in-unreal-engine).

### MetaHuman Creator

#### Turn Full-body Meshes into a MetaHuman Character, Ready to Animate

![Turn Full-body Meshes into a MetaHuman Character](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b9e3d012-ee87-49a0-96b9-23b2b95af989?resizing_type=fit)

Convert any human character mesh with arbitrary topology into a fully-rigged MetaHuman in a single workflow. This improved [Mesh to MetaHuman process](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/metahuman/metahuman-creator-import-tools-in-unreal-engine) conforms both head and body simultaneously, accepting input meshes of any topology and automatically generating results powered by the MetaHuman database.

**Key Features:**

- Combined head and body conforming in a single step.

- Accepts head and/or body mesh of any topology as input.

- Automatic results for human characters with manual control available for technical fixes.

- Ideal for characters created from scans, external GenAI/DCC tools, or existing character conversions.


Designed for humanoid characters only; the resulting character will adopt the MetaHuman topology and rig.

For more information on this feature, see [From Custom Mesh](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/metahuman/metahuman-creator-from-custom-mesh-tool-in-unreal-engine).

#### Achieve Higher Fidelity or Alternative Visual Styles with Full Control of Unbaked Textures

![Full Control of MetaHuman Unbaked Textures in UE](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/5dfdb155-1a31-4c62-850b-c3febe0b75c6?resizing_type=fit)

Assemble MetaHuman characters without baked materials and textures. This allows granular lookdev and texture control for artists wanting to match a specific look. Author unbaked texture and material assets using standard Unreal Engine editors or export textures to external DCC tools. Options are provided to then override with user-customized textures and materials in MetaHuman Creator.

**Key Features:**

- Full control over textures and materials for custom visual fidelity or aesthetic styles.

- Modified unbaked materials and textures can be applied as overrides in the MetaHuman Creator for users to still benefit from the material baking when running default assemblies.

- Standard Unreal Engine workflow using familiar asset editors.

- Export capabilities for external DCC authoring.


**Use Case:** Enables looks beyond MetaHuman Creator's built-in capabilities while maintaining performance optimization.

For more information, see [Unbaked Materials](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/metahuman/metahuman-creator-unbaked-assembly-in-unreal-engine).

#### Preview MetaHuman Characters Using Your Lighting Setup

![Preview MetaHuman Characters Using Your Lighting Setup in UE](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/5adcb461-59c0-41f5-8979-ae33cb8fe385?resizing_type=fit)

Create custom lighting scenes in MetaHuman Creator to preview characters in the context of your target environment. Define lighting setups using templates that include skydome hemispheres, post-processing volumes, and light groups, then use these custom scenes to validate visual fidelity while authoring.

**Key Features:**

- Preview characters in your target lighting environment directly in MetaHuman Creator.

- Close the gap between MetaHuman Creator previews and in-level appearance.

- Inspect and modify viewport render settings for precise control.

- Ideal for character artists, lighting artists, and lookdev teams.

- MetaHuman Creator viewport now fully supports Lumen too.


Custom scenes use templates rather than importing full-game levels; results may still require iterative refinement to match the exact in-engine appearance.

For more information, see [Custom Lighting Scenarios and Render Settings](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/metahuman/metahuman-custom-lighting-scenarios-and-render-settings-in-unreal-engine).

### MetaHuman Animator

#### Capture Body Animation from a Single Camera

​Capture body, or face and body performance, for a single actor from a single camera. This new experimental capability extends the accessibility of MetaHuman Animator from faces to bodies, removing the optical motion-capture stage as a barrier for content creators. Available as a standalone plugin on Fab and integrated directly into MetaHuman Animator, with the Live Link Face mobile apps updated to support body capture alongside face.​

**Key Features:**

- Body capture for a single actor from a single camera, with optional simultaneous face capture.

- Offline solve for high-fidelity results.

- Compatible with a wide range of consumer hardware including webcams and supported smartphones.

- Available as a standalone MetaHuman Animator Markerless Motion Capture plugin via Fab, and integrated as a capability of MetaHuman Animator inside Unreal Engine.

- Extended [capture guidelines](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/metahuman/metahuman-animator-performance-capture-guidelines-in-unreal-engine) included in documentation.


For more information on this feature, see [Animation from Mono Video Capture](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/metahuman/metahuman-animation-from-mono-video-capture-in-unreal-engine).

#### MetaHuman Animator Streamlined Batch Processing

![MetaHuman Animator Streamlined Batch Processing in UE](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/6c2eff14-e9ef-43fe-b9c6-03a8051f9ba0?resizing_type=fit)

MetaHuman Animator offers an improved API for batch processing large volumes of captured performance data. The updated workflow covers the full pipeline, end to end, from solve through animation review and export. Reference Blueprint examples will be included to extend or customize for your specific pipeline.

#### MetaHuman Animator Available on Linux and macOS

MetaHuman Animator now supports Linux and macOS, expanding the availability of the Unreal Engine editor and MetaHuman Creator across platforms. You can generate facial animation from performance capture on Linux and macOS, without requiring access to a Windows machine. However, body animation features are currently only available on Windows.

**Key Features:**

- Offline and real-time facial MetaHuman Animator functionality available on Linux and macOS.

- Platform parity with Unreal Engine editor and MetaHuman Creator.

- Real-time facial animation on Linux is only available using Live Link Face.


Editor-only solution; not a runtime or player-facing feature.

#### Improved MetaHuman Animator Solve and Curve Quality

![Improved MetaHuman Animator Solve and Curve Quality in UE](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/405b6cbb-9346-4c6b-b9c3-008db3dd5d93?resizing_type=fit)

New real-time and offline animation models deliver improved solve quality across a wider range of capture conditions, including varied camera angles, lens distortion, and infrared lighting. Audio-driven animation benefits from a new real-time model. Curve output is more animator-friendly, with cleaner activation on key poses for easier editing and refinement.

## Worldbuilding

### Mesh Terrain (Experimental)

![Mesh Terrain](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/0162bb50-b312-4b2c-9a22-e6ca1dd821a9?resizing_type=fit)

A next-generation mesh-based terrain solution to support large worlds using 3D modeling, layering, virtual texture, generic editor tools, variable tessellation, and Nanite. Our aim with this feature is to replace and remove the typical constraints of the current heightfield-only landscape solution in Unreal Engine.

For more information about this feature, see [Mesh Terrain](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/mesh-terrain-in-unreal-engine).

### Fast Geometry Streaming (Experimental)

In the **Fast Geometry Streaming** plugin, we included multiple new improvements for speed, stability, and use cases support, over the initial 5.6 release.

- Added decal, point, spot and rect lights components support.

- Added support for mesh paint textures in the static mesh component.

- Added more functionality in IPhysicsBodyInstanceOwnerResolver:

  - GetCollisionObjectType

  - GetCollisionEnabled

  - GetTransform

  - GetPhysicsObjectById

  - GetAllPhysicsObjects
- Fixed non-primitive components that were ignored from the transformation process.

- Fixed the FastGeoContainer not containing any physics.

- `FastGeoStreaming.ini` is now `DefaultFastGeoStreaming.ini`.

- Root component mobility is now preserved when the FastGeo runtime cell transformer creates a new replacement root component for a transformed component.

- Fixed primitives incorrectly showing when running PIE and the player is ejected.

- Fixed a MT issue in-editor.

- Removed unused EProxyCreationState::Pending and UFastGeoComponentEditorProxy.

- Refactored to simplify/clarify the interface of the fast geometry component.

- Fixed the WorldPartitionRuntimeCellTransformerISM duplicating instances for Blueprint actors that were not fully transformable.


Multiple additional fixes for crashes, threading, deadlocks and initialization are also part of this experimental release.

### World Partition Insights

We added world partition streaming debugging tools to Unreal Insights and Unreal Editor, making possible per-cell analysis and sessions playback.

### HLOD UX

We made the following improvements to world partition hierarchical level of details (HLODs).

**Functionality:**

- Added a batched deletion operation to reduce source control overhead.

- Now supports standalone HLODs when placing multiple instances of the same sub-world partition level.

- Added a perceptual difference heuristic option to update HLODs only when needed.

- Added support for new and deleted actors when building HLODs directly from a level in the editor.


**UX:**

- Build HLOD for Selection.

- Build HLOD for Selected Region through the world partition editor.


## Procedural Content Generation (PCG)

### Manual Editing

![Manual Editing](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/fc4670e8-8d31-4844-83a9-c2253bab87f9?resizing_type=fit)

In UE 5.8, we added non-destructive manual editing of PCG data and artifacts through selection, exclusion, modification and support for restoring data.

Individual nodes in the graphs can be marked for manual editing or temporarily overridden. A new Data Overrides window lists all overrides applied to an inspected node.

### Complex Attributes

Using arrays, structures, sets, and maps as metadata attribute values and overrides are now supported. This includes various operations to extract data in structures and arrays as well as array operations.

New Create Complex Constant and Add Complex Constant nodes are available to use in PCG graphs on top of graph parameters with complex types.

### Embedded Subgraphs

We added support for creating custom subgraphs, similar to Blueprint functions, stored and edited directly within a PCG graph.

### Graph Parameters Editor

You can now categorize, sort, group, and describe PCG parameters in the new parameters hierarchy editor tool.

### PCG Performance

Runtime:

- PCG GPU runtime scatter is now within the same performance range as the landscape GPU grass system, and was stress-tested on all platforms.

- Actor/component-less runtime generation


Editor:

- Added CRC and caching improvements when running a graph, reducing potential cache invalidation with increased efficiency.

- Improved ISM re-use logic when spawning large sets of static meshes.

- Made graph execution and scheduling improvements removing contention and bottlenecks.


### PCG UX

We continue to make UX improvements when working with PCG, these are latest changes:

- **Contextual filtering:** When adding a new node by dragging from any typed pin, the node palette is automatically filtered to supported operations, with options to include conversions or disable filtering entirely.

- **HLSL kernels:** You can now create attributes directly from the HLSL kernel rather than in the node settings.

- **HLSL editor:** You can now set font size.

- **Data viewport:** You can now edit manual overrides from the PCG editor's data viewport


### PCG Nodes and Operators

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we also introduce multiple native PCG elements and new options including:

- **Metadata array operations:** Most useful operations for arrays (make, add, add unique, contains, and more).

- **Align points:** Snap points position and rotation against the bounds of another point on any given axis and spatial referential.

- **Scene Capture:** The Scene Capture node now supports input transforms allowing captures to be taken from any direction and adding extra flexibility for GPU sampling.

- **Create / Add Complex Constant:** Use these nodes to create or add any complex attribute type directly in the graph.

- **Apply Spline to Component:** Writes the PCG spline data onto an existing Spline component reference. Useful for applying changes on existing splines in-editor.

- **Teleport Actors and Components:** Gives you a method to apply a transform to any actor or component reference in the world. Useful for a new level-based PCG workflow to apply an instant operation in-editor.

- **Get Class from Attribute:** Gets the class from a soft object reference and returns it as an attribute.

- **Get Editor Cameras:** Returns the current visible editor viewport cameras as points to use for various in-editor operations.

- **Set Materials On Dynamic Mesh:** Apply material to dynamic mesh data.


### Procedural Vegetation Editor (Experimental)

![Procedural Vegetation Editor](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/cf45c48c-5c37-40be-b043-e377b0e44d60?resizing_type=fit)

The **Procedural Vegetation Editor** is an experimental plugin to create and edit vegetation meshes, supporting Nanite foliage, directly within Unreal Engine. With UE 5.8, we introduce some core new functionality that greatly expands the capabilities of PVE, enabling growth directly in the editor without the need for imported recipes, along with numerous other improvements.

- Growth Node

- Seed Generation

- Skeletal Extraction from 3D Mesh or 2D image/Atlas

- Foliage Grafting

- Object Avoidance and Carving

- Trimming- branch loops, displacement tessellation

- Mesher Improvements

- Visualization Modes

- Trunk Material Compositor


For more information on this feature, see [Procedural Vegetation Editor](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/procedural-vegetation-editor-pve-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.7).

## Framework

### StateTree Starting States and Compiler Extensions

![StateTree Starting States and Compiler Extensions](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/8841ccd1-6048-45c9-9302-d59fb2ba716a?resizing_type=fit)

**State Tree** gets a flexibility boost in UE 5.8.

We improved authoring workflows; trees can now define their starting state.

A new Compiler Manager helps streamline iteration, and the editor now tracks when trees are out of date so it’s clearer when a recompile is needed.

Property binding is more robust and now allows binding to be easily reversed, making it straightforward to move data from one completed task to another.

For more information on this feature, see [Statetree](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/state-tree-in-unreal-engine).

### Mass Framework: Faster, Modular, and Built for Scale

![Mass Framework: Faster, Modular, and Built for Scale](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/3749001b-d485-4dc3-a195-a30945b62aca?resizing_type=fit)

**Mass**, our data-oriented entity system, gets a major overhaul.

**Mass Signals** are now part of the core engine, and entities can be created off the game thread thanks to archetype-based, lock-free scheduling. A new sparse/virtual fragment system reduces memory use and allows optional fragments and tags to be added or removed without triggering costly archetype changes.

We completely overhauled Mass processor execution and dependency resolution to better take advantage of multi-core CPUs, resulting in safer and faster execution on modern hardware. This is supported by more granular scheduling and thread-safe observer notifications.

A new **MassCore** module further simplifies adoption by separating the core entity system from the broader MassGameplay stack.

For more information on this feature, see [MassEntity](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/mass-entity-in-unreal-engine).

### Navigation: Per-Mesh Control Over Walkable Surfaces

![Navigation: Per-Mesh Control Over Walkable Surfaces](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/1d123943-8a63-4c47-b2a5-67e1b1ef33db?resizing_type=fit)

Static meshes can now define their own walkable areas during navmesh generation, giving designers more control over how AI navigates the world. You can assign per-mesh area costs to static geometry—for example, marking a couch so AI prefers to walk around it instead of over it.

This is enabled per mesh through a flag and area class setting on NavCollision, with support carried through the full Recast generation pipeline.

### Iris: Production-Ready Replication System

![Iris: Production-Ready Replication System](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/f35902a7-a1cd-479e-9931-d2e7cf2b99ce?resizing_type=fit)

**Iris** is now production-ready for licensees in UE 5.8.

Alongside that milestone, we added a range of improvements that focus on stability and day-to-day usability. We improved protocol mismatch handling so clients get clearer errors when out of sync with the server, and new warnings help catch object lifecycle issues earlier. Serialization, cull distance handling, and diagnostics have all been refined, and RPC DoS detection has been re-enabled.

Iris also moves closer to the engine’s broader direction, with added support for Scene Graph integration and RemoteObjects RPC routing.

For more information on this feature, see [Iris Replication System](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/iris-replication-system-in-unreal-engine).

### Mover: Improved Physics, Animation, and Networking

![Mover: Improved Physics, Animation, and Networking](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/9cc6a52a-5b31-4077-9568-63caa1047001?resizing_type=fit)

**Mover** receives a broad update across core movement, networking, animation, and ChaosMover.

Core movement modes get a wide range of fixes and improvements, including NavWalking support for Detour Crowd, better based movement for scenarios like moving platforms or rocking boats, and improved root motion and montage handling.

Layered moves can now be scheduled ahead of time for better synchronization, while rollback and prediction support have been expanded.

Networking also improves with optional Iris replication support in Network Prediction and adaptive time dilation to reduce client predict-ahead.

ChaosMover adds trajectory prediction for motion-matching workflows, deeper Chaos Visual Debugger integration, and broader support for sim-driven montages, layered moves, gameplay tags, and instant movement effects.

Together, these changes continue the architectural work toward moving Mover out of Experimental status while improving stability across movement modes, prediction, resimulation, and animation-driven workflows.

### Unified Input System: Common UI and Enhanced Input

![Unified Input System: Common UI and Enhanced Input](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/2ccf186e-26e5-4002-8b29-bceb6b0cc3da?resizing_type=fit)

We streamlined input workflows in UE 5.8 with the unification of Enhanced Input and Common Input/UI. This simplifies cross-platform input handling, removes the need for duplicate data assets, and makes debugging more straightforward.

The update also includes a range of improvements across input handling, including more reliable event processing, better widget binding behavior, expanded virtual key support, and fixes for trigger edge cases.

New tooling, such as an Input Debugger for Enhanced Input UI and added extensibility, makes it easier to build and troubleshoot input-driven experiences.

## Developer Iteration

### Incremental Cooking (Beta)

**Incremental Cooking** continues as a beta feature for UE 5.8. Improvements to determinism further reduces the need to recook unmodified assets notably with DDC and structured data variations.

Incremental Cooking helps you to iterate faster on your target devices by reducing overall cooking time. Cook processes automatically analyze asset changes against output stored in Zen Server and only cook new updates made to your project's assets. This works across all native engine assets including Blueprints and World Partition tiles.

### Zenserver as Cooked Output Store

Zenserver as Cooked Output Store is now enabled by default. This also has meaning for Zenserver Streaming being used automatically by workflows in Unreal Editor when launching the game / client on devices, and staging container files (pak / iostore) remains available and supported for non-iteration workflows. To ensure this functions with remote devices, Zenserver responds to remote requests, but only if they supply a pre-generated key for authorization.

- Existing projects that have the use of Zen store disabled in their project settings will not use Zenserver as a cooked output store. They will need to manually change the setting in the project settings to enable it.

- For professional development use cases, projects should set LimitProcessLifetime=false in the Zen.AutoLaunch section of the DefaultEngine.ini configuration file so that Zenserver is not starting and stopping frequently. This requires consideration from automated / build processes to ensure that Zenserver continuing to run happens in a way that doesn’t interfere with automated / build processes.

- The AllowRemoteNetworkService config key has been renamed and changed to RemoteNetworkService and doesn’t accept true / false, and instead uses the following values:

  - None rejects remote requests to the local UE-launched Zenserver.

  - Unsecured accepts remote requests to the local UE-launched Zenserver if they contain an authorization key in their header that matches a UE-generated key.

  - GeneratedStaticKey is the default value.

For more information on this topic, see [Zenserver as Cooked Output Store](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/using-zen-storage-server-as-cooked-output-store-for-unreal-engine) and [Zenserver Streaming](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/how-to-use-zenserver-streaming-to-play-on-target-in-unreal-engine).

### Horde - Performance Reporting (Experimental)

![Horde - Performance Reporting (Experimental)](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/c429e45c-42d4-4145-bb06-a2e0ffa38d23?resizing_type=fit)

Improvements to **Horde Analytics** tooling continues in UE 5.8 as an Experimental feature with improvements to dashboard UX for job steps (CPU, memory usage) and job health observability.

We've also introduced a new view in Horde which shows runtime trends outputted from the Automated Performance Tests framework (APT) and the Perf Report Tool (csvprofilers), highlighting key metrics such as GPU/CPU times, peak memory usage and hitch reports so regressions can be spotted. This currently relies on users having their own database store model.

## Audio

### Audio Insights (Production Ready)

![Audio Insights](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/1564890c-f86c-4a13-9119-e0c41d450800?resizing_type=fit)

**Audio Insights** received a big update with new features and improvements in UE 5.8, expanding its diagnostic capabilities across loudness metering, signal flow visualization, live event monitoring, and data plotting — alongside numerous stability, UX, and standalone app improvements.

- **Loudness Metering:** A dedicated loudness meter tracks momentary, short-term, and integrated loudness values along with loudness range and true peak values, target max values and clipping indicators, processed on the engine and streamed into both the editor and standalone app.

- **Signal Flow Visualizer:** A new tab that traces the instantaneous audio signal graph from its source through submixes to the output device, displaying mixing values at each stage to find attenuation or routing issues. Displays cached data as well for offline forensic analysis.

- **Timeline Cache Controls:** Dynamic controls over display playhead synchronizing data display for a single timestamp across several dashboards of data.

- **Control Bus and Modulation Visibility:** The Control Bus tab now surfaces Control Bus Mixes as sources alongside individual buses, and the Modulation tab filters down to only active control bus columns to reduce noise.

- **Live Monitoring:** Audio Insights can now display trace data in real-time without saving a trace file, eliminating disk space concerns during long monitoring sessions. Both editor and standalone versions (via Unreal Insights) are supported.

- **Event Log:** A new dockable Events tab provides a live, scrollable chronological log of sound start, stop, and other audio events. Events are text-filterable, time-selectable to sync other visualizations, and double-clickable to navigate directly to the corresponding instance in the Sounds tab.

- **Plots:** A dedicated Plots tab consolidates per-sound parameter plotting with improved rendering, corrected color continuity across trace pauses, and fixed display artifacts in standalone.

- **Standalone and Cache Improvements:** The data cache manager now works in standalone sessions, trace data can be saved to a file directly from dashboard caches, and the cache size is now user-configurable via settings.


For more information on this feature, see [Audio Insights](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/audio-insights-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.7).

### Audio Subtitles (Beta)

![Audio Subtitles](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b4b35749-4e97-4d50-a8c0-c87023ac8db2?resizing_type=fit)

**Audio subtitles** are required for accessibility – dialogue systems, closed captioning, and voice chat. We promoted the plugin from Experimental to Beta status, reflecting its increased stability and feature completeness.

- Subtitles now display correctly for all sound types triggered within a MetaSound graph, including nested MetaSounds.

- Per-platform subtitle display overrides are now supported, allowing different widget placement and styling for platforms such as mobile or Nintendo Switch where screen layout differs.

- Subtitles in a Level Sequence can now be previewed directly in the editor without entering Play In Editor (PIE), making iteration on subtitle timing faster.

- Subtitle duration can now be overridden per locale, automatically using the duration of the locale-specific sound wave when a localized asset is present.

- A new QueueSingleSubtitle Blueprint and C++ function replaces the older QueueSubtitle (now deprecated). A companion function, QueueSubtitlesFromAsset, queues all subtitle lines stored in an asset in a single call with correct timing offsets applied automatically.

- We added a Comment field to subtitle assets for internal notes visible in the editor but not shown at runtime.

- Various UX improvements and bugfixes.


### Waveform Editor (Beta)

Sound designers need powerful editing tools without leaving the engine. We are continuing to improve the Waveform Editor with deeper control over fades and workflow refinements to reduce round-trips to external audio tools.

- **Fades** are now decoupled from trim. A new Fade transformation allows any number of independent fade regions — each with their own fade-in and fade-out — to be placed anywhere on the waveform, completely independent of the TrimFade region. Trim fade-in and fade-out curve types can also now be set directly from the toolbar, with right-click context menus on fade handles providing additional curve shape options. Scrolling on a fade handle adjusts the curve slope.

- **Reimport** is now available from the editor toolbar, with three modes: reimport and overwrite transformations (including marker and loop region data from cue and smpl chunks), reimport keeping existing transformations, or reimport from a new file entirely.

- A new **Launch Transformations** setting helps you pre-configure which transformations are automatically applied when opening a SoundWave that has none. This removes repetitive setup steps for standard editing workflows.

- When transformation changes are applied, the **SoundWave's LUFS and Sample Peak metadata** now update automatically to reflect the transformed waveform, keeping asset metadata accurate without requiring a manual refresh.

- Additional keyboard shortcuts for marker navigation:

  - G skips the playhead to the next marker.

  - F/B selects the next/previous loop marker.

  - H snaps the playhead to the nearest zero crossing.

  - Enter stops playback and rewinds to the start.

  - Shift+Space resets the playhead to the beginning of the file without affecting playback state.
- Many other usability, UX and UI improvements.


To get started with this feature, see [Waveform Editor Quick Start](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/waveform-editor-quick-start-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.6).

### MetaSound Node Configuration (Experimental)

**MetaSound Node Configuration**, introduced in UE 5.7, is now expanded in UE 5.8 with new tools that reduce boilerplate for developers and improve the editing experience for designers.

- **Dynamic Interface Node Configuration:** A new built-in FMetaSoundDynamicInterfaceNodeConfiguration struct automatically manages sub-interface instance counts and variant type selection based on a node's FClassInterface definition. Developers no longer need to write custom per-node configuration structs for the common case of exposing sub-interface counts or variant pin types — the Details panel now surfaces these controls automatically as dropdowns and count fields.


- **Node Update Transform API:** A new, more structured API for authoring node update scripts gives developers fine-grained control over how nodes migrate when their interface changes across major versions. Custom update logic is now associated with a specific major version and runs after minor-version and interface updates have been applied, ensuring predictable ordering. An example migration — updating the biquad filter's default bandwidth from 1.0 to 2.0 for newly-placed nodes while preserving the legacy default for existing content — demonstrates the pattern.


- **Sub-Interface Layout Serialization:** Sub-interface layout information is now correctly reconstituted when deserializing MetaSounds, resolving cases where vertex name collisions and layout loss occurred on certain platforms.


- **API Stability:** FClassInterface exits its experimental designation in UE 5.8. FNodeClassMetadata::DefaultInterface now accepts FClassInterface directly (replacing FVertexInterface), and deprecated input/output node creation helpers have been removed from IDataTypeRegistry. Developers building Node Configuration integrations can treat this as the stable public API surface going forward.


### MetaSound Templates (Experimental)

**MetaSound Templates** is a new Experimental feature in UE 5.8 that gives audio programmers the means to create reusable, property-driven MetaSound generation logic that sound designers can use enabling rapid iteration without ever having to touch the graph.

- A **Template** is a C++ defined UStruct that can procedurally configure and rebuild a MetaSound graph, its interface, and inputs any time a designer changes one of its exposed properties.

  - Templates can limit what Designers see to only the properties the template author chose to expose; the underlying graph, member list, page options, and more, can optionally be hidden entirely.

  - The programmer defines a small set of parameters they want designers to control — a list of sounds, a pitch range, a filter cutoff — and the Template's code handles configuring the given options into a valid MetaSound graph.
- From the MetaSound Editor, designers select a template from the new Template toolbar dropdown and edit its properties in the MetaSound Details panel.

  - Converting a templated MetaSound back to a standard one (preserving the last generated graph state) is also supported.

  - A template can also ship a fully custom UMG widget tab built on Unreal's MVVM framework, providing a purpose-built interface — sliders, previews, array editors — instead of or alongside the default MetaSound panels.
- A **Randomizer template** ships with UE 5.8 as a reference implementation. It picks randomly from a designer-specified list of Sound Waves, applies a pitch offset within a configurable semitone range, and supports both one-shot and looping playback modes. It is hidden by default in UE 5.8, but serves as a working code example for template authors.


### Format / Channel Agnostic Types (CAT) (Experimental)

- **Full Pipeline Integration:** CAT output is now wired through MetaSoundSource meaning a MetaSound graph can produce a CAT signal and deliver it directly to the audio engine. The channel format can be automatically determined by looking at the sound waves set on the MetaSoundSource inputs.


- **Data-Defined Audio Formats:** Custom channel configurations can now be declared as first-class audio formats and used directly within graphs. This enables teams to define and work with non-standard or proprietary speaker layouts without forking engine code.


- **Ambisonics and Transcoding:** First-order Ambisonics is now a built-in CAT format. Transcoding between Discrete and Ambisonics formats is handled automatically at graph boundaries, so spatial audio workflows no longer require manual conversion nodes.


#### New Nodes for Experimentation

- **Wave Player 2.0:** A next-generation wave player reimplemented on top of the CAT foundation utilizing experimental sound asset container.

- **CAT Mixer:** A dedicated mixing node for combining multichannel CAT signals within a graph

- **Grain Player:** A grain synthesis playback node built on the CAT pipeline

- **Multiply**: The Multiply node gains new CAT-aware variants:


  - CAT × float

  - CAT × CAT


Multichannel signals can now be scaled and modulated without collapsing to mono first, enabling per-channel gain, ring modulation, and envelope shaping directly on multichannel buses.

- **Ladder Filter:** We ported the Ladder Filter to process both standard AudioBuffer and CAT signals. The existing mono filter path is preserved; the CAT path handles multichannel audio with independent per-channel filtering. This conversion also serves as the reference implementation for porting additional MetaSound DSP nodes to CAT.


### Audio in Sequencer

Sound designers using Sequencer for cinematics, gameplay sequences, and rendering frequently hit friction around audio mixing control, default behaviors that don't match expectations, and audio quality issues in exported renders. In UE 5.8 we are shipping a significant set of improvements across three areas.

#### Control Bus and Control Bus Mix Tracks

- Two new Sequencer tracks bring Audio Modulation directly into the timeline.

  - The **Control Bus Track** makes it possible for any Audio Modulation Control Bus — volume, pitch, filter cutoff, or any custom modulation parameter — to be keyframed and animated over time within a sequence.

  - The Control Bus Mix Track provides a way to activate and deactivate a pre-defined Control Bus Mix (a set of modulation values applied together) at specific points in the sequence, enabling precise and repeatable audio mix states tied to cinematic events.

#### Playback and Section Behavior Improvements

- We redefined Audio section looping behavior to align more closely with typical sound designer intent; users define if a sound will play to completion rather than reusing concepts of KeepState or RestoreState when the section is finished, and Looping was renamed as Repeating to distinguish between section on game frame boundaries and asset looping on sample boundaries.

- Audio sections no longer auto-expand when keyframes are added outside their bounds.

- MetaSound integration enables more reliable playback of MetaSound sources.

- The audio evaluation system has been improved to avoid unnecessary stop-and-restart when the playhead context jumps, resulting in smoother scrubbing and pause/resume behavior.


#### Movie Render Queue Audio Improvements

- MRQ now supports expanded submix selection for audio export, giving you direct control over which submix is recorded rather than being limited to the default output.

- We fixed audio popping, gaps, and repeats that previously occurred at camera cut boundaries; the audio component is now paused and resumed across cuts rather than stopped and restarted, eliminating sample-level discontinuities in rendered output.


### WASAPI

In Unreal Engine 5.8, we switched the default audio backend on Windows from XAudio2 to **WASAPI**. The new AudioMixerWasapi module is now selected automatically; XAudio2 remains available as an opt-in fallback. The same backend is also used on Xbox. No changes are required on the developers end. All content should behave the same — only the layer that talks to the operating system has changed.

**Why we made the switch:**

- Future-proofing. Building on a supported, actively-maintained Windows API instead of a legacy one.

- Better latency capabilities. Direct access to the lower-level API gives the audio mixer more control over buffer scheduling.

- More robust device handling. The WASAPI backend now includes full device-swap support — plugging or unplugging headphones, switching the Windows default device, or having audio drivers force a device change is handled cleanly by the engine.

- Quality and reliability improvements. Over the course of the 5.8 cycle, the audio team hardened the backend against a long list of real-world device-change, format-negotiation, and shutdown edge cases discovered in production. The result is a more stable Windows audio path out of the box.


**What you should know:**

- This is a Module, not a plugin. WASAPI ships as the AudioMixerWasapi module inside the engine. There's nothing to enable or install.

- Device swap is supported. Headset connect/disconnect, default-device changes, and sample-rate changes are all handled by the backend.

- Opting out (fallback to XAudio2). If you hit a project-specific issue, you can revert to the previous backend by adding the following to your project's `Config/Windows/WindowsEngine.ini`:




```ini

```





Copy full snippet(2 lines long)


We recommend reporting any issue you encounter so it can be addressed before XAudio2 is eventually removed.


## Platform

### Mobile Renderer

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we advance the mobile renderer and expand access to higher-quality rendering features on supported devices.

UE 5.8 delivers:

- Multi-pass deferred rendering as the default path across mobile platforms (with forward rendering still available as an opt-in).

- Broader use of GBuffer and depth data.

- Mobile support for SSAO, SSR, deferred decals, contact shadows, and higher-quality water rendering.


In UE 5.8 we also introduce half-precision (FP16) shader usage in targeted materials and global shader passes, improving performance while preserving visual quality.

Together, these changes raise visual fidelity and scalability on high-end mobile hardware while preserving performance and giving teams more headroom to tune quality levels.

### Android Platform Support

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we deliver targeted Android platform improvements focused on input support and iteration speed.

UE 5.8 delivers:

- Improved controller mapping support.

- Simpler automated setup of developer workstations using Turnkey.


These changes improve developer productivity and platform robustness for teams building and testing Android projects.

### Preview Platform

In Unreal Engine 5.8, we improve the visual fidelity of the **Preview Platform** feature so visuals displayed in the Editor more closely match the look and behavior of target hardware.

Teams can catch visual issues earlier and reduce the cost of switching to device for iteration.

For more information on this feature, see [Using Preview Platform](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/using-preview-platform-in-unreal-engine)

### Keyboard and Mouse Support for iOS and iPadOS

In Unreal Engine 5.8, we add full keyboard and mouse support for iOS and iPadOS, giving creators and players a way to interact with projects using standard desktop input devices. This brings input behavior on iPad and iOS closer to macOS parity, improving usability for development, testing, and gameplay scenarios where keyboard and mouse are expected.

Projects running on iOS and iPadOS can now be interacted with in a consistent, desktop-like way when appropriate, reducing platform-specific friction when targeting Apple ecosystems.

### Gesture Events for iOS and Android (Experimental)

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we introduce an experimental gesture event system that bridges to the native gesture recognizers on iOS and Android and surfaces their events directly to the engine. Pinch, swipe, rotate, and pan are recognized with the same accuracy, timing, and began/changed/ended state transitions that native apps get, removing per-platform touch-handling code and giving developers a consistent way to drive touch-based interactions across mobile.

### iOS Application Extensions

In Unreal Engine 5.8, we add first-class support for iOS App Extensions through a new `.uappex` control file. Project authors can now declare extensions such as Notification Service or Background Assets alongside their UE project, and UnrealBuildTool generates the corresponding Xcode App Extension target automatically — no manual post-generation Xcode editing required.

### Unreal Engine Remote

**Unreal Engine Remote** is a companion app that lets developers preview and test mobile input without building or deploying to a physical device. 5.8 expands the app to Android (previously iOS-only) and switches the streaming backend to Pixel Streaming 2, so a live Play in Editor session from UE5 or a Mobile Preview session from Unreal Editor for Fortnite can be streamed to a mobile device — mirroring the in-game experience on device and reporting touch and gesture inputs back in real time.

This means teams can:

- Validate mobile input behavior directly from a preview session.

- Iterate on touch controls without a full device build.

- Test across both UE5 and UEFN workflows using the same app, on both iOS and Android.


UE Remote shortens the mobile development loop, giving developers a fast, accurate impression of how input feels on mobile hardware without the cost of repeated on-device deployments.

For more information on this feature, see [Using Unreal Engine Remote with Remote Session](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/using-unreal-engine-remote-with-remote-session).

### Steam Frame Support (Experimental)

Together with Valve we have implemented experimental support for their next XR platform: [https://store.steampowered.com/sale/steamframe](https://store.steampowered.com/sale/steamframe)

`bPackageForOpenXRImmersive` is a new setting that defaults to true in the VR Template.

### Stereo Layer Underlays

In UE 5.8, OpenXR stereo layers can now be drawn behind the main scene. This opens up XR effects that used to require engine modifications or vendor-specific plugins.

Before UE 5.8, Unreal Engine's OpenXR support always drew stereo layers on top of the projection layer (the rendered UE world), and face-locked layers always sat above world-locked ones. That fixed order made true "underlays" — layers that appear behind the environment — impossible out of the box, even though the OpenXR spec itself just takes an ordered list of layers with no such rule.

This change replaces the fixed order with one driven by layer priority, matching how OpenXR works. It adds two new settings:

- `xr.OpenXRProjectionLayerPriority` (default = 0). The priority of the projection layer. Any stereo layer with a lower priority is drawn behind it; anything higher is drawn in front, as before.

- `xr.OpenXRSortFaceLockedLayersAboveOtherLayers` (off by default) — when on, face-locked layers always draw above everything else, regardless of priority. This matches the old behavior.


To restore the pre-UE 5.8 order, set `xr.OpenXRSortFaceLockedLayersAboveOtherLayers=1` and set `xr.OpenXRProjectionLayerPriority` to a value lower than every stereo layer priority in your project (for example, -2147483648, the minimum 32-bit integer). Existing projects keep working with no changes.

GitHub changelist for details ( [connected account required](https://www.unrealengine.com/ue-on-github)): [https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine/commit/83641b6ac8b243d9858f54bafe1937f0accb4b6f](https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine/commit/83641b6ac8b243d9858f54bafe1937f0accb4b6f)

For more information on this feature, see [OpenXR Stereo Layers](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/openxr-stero-layers-in-unreal-engine).

### PICO Controller OpenXR Plugin

The **PICO Controller** plugin adds support for PICO's OpenXR interaction profiles XR\_BD\_controller\_interaction and XR\_BD\_ultra\_controller\_interaction.

The plugin is enabled by default in the VR Template and PICO controller bindings have been configured for the Input Mapping Contexts.

### iOS Shader Model 6 (Experimental)

In Unreal Engine 5.8, we add experimental Shader Model 6 (SM6) support on iOS, integrating Apple's Metal Shader Converter library to unlock advanced GPU features on Apple Silicon.

UE 5.8 delivers:

- A dedicated iOS SM6 shader platform variant alongside the existing Metal paths

- Wave intrinsics (SIMD-group operations) for more efficient GPU compute algorithms

- Native 16-bit (FP16) shader types to improve ALU throughput on Apple Silicon


Support targets A15 and newer Apple Silicon and ships as experimental, with the existing Metal rendering paths preserved for broader device coverage. Validation of SM6-gated rendering features such as improved deferred techniques and higher-quality compute paths is underway and will land in subsequent releases.

## Content Pipeline

### UI rework - Interchange Import Dialog UI

![UI rework - Interchange Import Dialog UI](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/df921319-d999-4eaf-a19a-00d002c171cd?resizing_type=fit)

The **Interchange Framework** is highly customizable and subsequently the window dialogs to configure Interchange and to import data are overwhelming with options.

The goal of the upcoming releases is to simplify the UI. In UE 5.8, we regrouped and renamed all options related to asset type conversion for better clarity, while material import options have clearer control of creation of material versus use of existing materials.

For more information on this feature, see [Interchange Framework](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/interchange-framework-in-unreal-engine).

### FBX Import Performance

![FBX Import Performance](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/455d843d-f0de-4cf0-8e90-2d3f8ea19c9d?resizing_type=fit)

While glTF and USD usage intensifies, FBX remains the main data format to import 3D models in Unreal Engine. This is why we introduced an alternative library to improve user experience with this format.

In UE 5.8, we performed stabilization work to support for the uFBX library (Experimental); it noticeably reduces import import times especially on heavy `.fbx` files containing large meshes. Users with multi -cores CPUs will also notice improvement for files with a large number of meshes.

In alignment with USD, Unreal will now preserve nodes visibility from `.fbx` files, when importing into level, and apply it on the "hidden in game" property.

## USD Asset Pre-Generation

![USD Asset Pre-Generation](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b30d990d-2d85-46c9-ae27-0f0d5449cd14?resizing_type=fit)

USD scenes are often composed recursively from multiple referenced USD files. The current USD Interchange import workflow processes these compositions in isolation, resulting in flattened imports and unnecessary duplication of asset data.

The new USD Pregen framework introduces a robust system for discovering, tracking, and persisting relationships between referenced USD assets and their corresponding Unreal Engine representations.

This feature is experimental in UE 5.8. The key benefits are:

- Reduced asset duplication

- Composition- and asset-aware processing

- Granular processing

- Configurable framework


### USD Import with Interchange

![USD Import with Interchange](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b96f22b5-eb16-43d0-ab83-f00f40d42130?resizing_type=fit)

USD is a versatile scene description file format with a growing adoption across the 3D industry.

We added USD to the list of file formats supported by the Interchange framework in 5.5. Content creators benefit from more control over the import process and can now add custom processing steps for asset import of USD files, similar to the Interchange capabilities that are already available with other formats such as FBX.

In UE 5.8, the support for USD through Interchange is considered production ready for asset import and experimental for level import. We added support for:

- Ordering of schema handlers; the ordered list of schema handlers used when loading a USD file is exposed and editable.

- Support for custom schema translator; USD translator can be extended in code to support custom schemas.

- A mechanism to add new render context.

- A Nanite build settings schema.

- All groom attributes.

- Collapsing (parity with legacy USD import).

- Chaos Cloth.


## Editor

### Editor Gizmo System

![Editor Gizmo System](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/843aa244-7e0f-46c6-b22b-d64c15d55ba8?resizing_type=fit)

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we introduce a new **Editor Gizmo System** designed to deliver a more consistent and flexible interaction experience across the editor. Built on top of the Interactive Tools Framework, the new system consolidates multiple legacy gizmo implementations into a single framework used across viewports and tools. This unification improves reliability, interaction consistency, and extensibility for developers building tools within the editor.

The redesigned gizmos also include a range of visual and usability improvements inspired by workflows familiar to artists and level designers from tools like Maya and Blender. With improved hit targets, clearer visual feedback, customizable interaction presets, and enhanced precision controls, the new system provides a faster and more predictable workflow for manipulating actors and assets.

For more information on this feature, see [Transforming Actors](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/transforming-actors-in-unreal-engine).

#### Visual and Interaction Improvements

- **Refined Gizmo Design:** Thinner visual profile with improved hit targets for more accurate selection and interaction.

- **Improved Hover and Interaction Feedback:** Clear highlighting when hovering or interacting with axes and planes.

- **Planar Handles Repositioned:** Planar movement axes are positioned further from the center, improving accessibility and reducing accidental selections.

- **Expanded Screen-Space Movement Handle:** Larger center movement square for easier screen-space translations.

- **Axis Visibility Improvements:** Axes temporarily hide during interaction to improve visual clarity.

- **Improved Scaling Behavior:** Gizmos now operate more reliably from all viewing angles, enabling more predictable scaling interactions.


#### Precision & Movement Feedback

- **Numeric Delta Overlays:** Real-time overlays display movement, rotation, or scale deltas during interaction.

- **Delta Line Indicators:** Visual lines indicate how far an object has been translated from its original position.

- **Rotation Delta Line:** Rotation interactions display a visual delta line similar to Blender, improving precision when rotating from greater distances.


#### Snapping & Interaction Enhancements

- **Snapping State Indicator:** The gizmo center icon now visually indicates when snapping is enabled.

- **Temporary Snapping Controls:** Quickly toggle position, rotation, scale, or surface snapping while holding a modifier key.

- **Viewport Boundary Interaction:** Continue manipulating actors even when the cursor moves outside the viewport bounds.


#### Customization and Workflow Presets

- **Interaction Presets:** Choose from multiple interaction styles:

  - Default Unreal Engine interaction

  - Classic Unreal interaction

  - Maya-style interaction
- **Customizable Gizmo Behavior:** Increased flexibility for teams to configure interactions based on their preferred workflow.


#### Precision Controls

- **Precision Mode:** Temporarily slow down transformations for fine adjustments.

- **Nudge Mode:** Incrementally adjust translation, rotation, or scale for controlled edits.


### Preview Scene Improvements

![Preview Scene Improvements](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/f7353edf-c929-40fc-9b6b-665bad3df65b?resizing_type=fit)

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we expand the **Preview Scene** system with new customization and workflow improvements for asset editors. These updates give users greater control over how assets are presented during preview, making it easier to evaluate materials, meshes, and lighting conditions directly within the editor.

#### Customization Enhancements

- **Custom Floor Mesh Support:** Configure a custom floor mesh in preview scenes to better match the environment where assets will be used.

- **Custom Floor Material:** Apply custom materials to the preview floor for improved context when reviewing assets.


### Workflow Improvements

- **Layout Improvements:** Profile management has been moved to the top of the Tab for easier access.

- **Preview Profile Cycling :** Quickly cycle between Advanced Preview Scene profiles using a keyboard shortcut, giving users a way to rapidly switch between lighting and environment setups when evaluating assets.


### Material Preview Editor Improvements

![Material Preview Editor Improvements](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/e77d86c4-cafe-4fa6-9fa5-b1cd1fe64629?resizing_type=fit)

With Unreal Engine 5.8, we introduce several improvements to the **Material Preview Editor** to support faster look development and more flexible preview workflows. These updates make it easier to evaluate materials using familiar preview meshes and quickly test assets directly within the preview environment.

#### Preview Enhancements
